nodes.title: The child never sees a piece being made (171d1db6). StudioStage has no 'making' phase: no '{T} is making this' chip, no pencil skeleton of the unfinished piece, no streamed-partial veil, no sparkle. While a slot is planning / building / ready, the stage keeps the last finished piece (inert) or the calm ground. Reversal: if the owner wants a visible 'coming' cue, it is a calm one-line cue in her words, never on the stage.

Round 7 D8 amends dc-r4c-studio-v2-off-child-path: a Studio v2 piece is served wherever its certificate passes AT THE DEVICE'S CLASS (p412, l1366). On the 360 phone, where its 1000-unit world is too small to play, it is served as its board twin, or not at all (tray-gate.js certifyForTray, cert 'catalogue-twin'). Reversal: per-device owner sign-off finds a certified class unusable; that class goes back to off (serveByViewport false) without code.

md.decisions:
## dc-r7-studio-no-build-state — no build state on the child's screen (2026-11-04)

OWNER-RESET: the child never sees 'Asha is making this', skeletons or veils. The stage shows only finished pieces. While the next one is made, the last finished piece stays up, inert, or the calm ground does.

## dc-r7-studio-v2-device-class-serving — serve Studio v2 where certified (2026-11-04)

Round 4 kept Studio v2 off the child path unless a piece was playable and certified at all three sizes. No piece was, so the authored explainers and games never reached a child. Round 7 decision D8 serves a piece wherever it is certified at the device's own class. On the 360 phone it is served as its board twin until the portrait relayout (C1 item 13). This amends dc-r4c-studio-v2-off-child-path.
md.measurements:
## ms-r7-studio-v2-servable (2026-11-04, n = 1,142 catalogue rows)

Under D8, from the existing per-class certificates: p412 1,007, l1366 1,071, p360 1,062 (as the board twin). Before: 0. Per-device visual sign-off by the owner is still pending.

## ms-r7-board-first-coverage (2026-11-04, n = 250 class 4-7 topics)

The board-first rung already picks a board before her line on 98% of first explain moves and 88.8% of subject-less picture asks (the maths misses are kit boards that are text, not a drawing). What remains is live: a picked board refused against her real line. GET /api/studio/timing now counts those outcomes per replica.
